stops.note: the city of Ancyra (modern Ankara) was named after it; Pausanias says King Midas's anchor was still shown there
early Christians painted the anchor in the Roman catacombs as a veiled symbol of hope
borrowed early from Latin; the -ch- spelling is a later imitation of the misspelling anchora
a news 'anchor', the linchpin of a broadcast, dates from the 1950s in US television

current_meaning: a heavy object that holds a ship in place; a news presenter
